problems: The picture: the mast doesn't come out of the deck. Its foot sits at the back edge of the deck, beside the far rear wheel, and the pole leans backward and away from the planks. Nothing ties it down: no step, no stays, no ropes.

The picture: the sail is a flat board hanging beside the mast. It isn't laced or hoisted onto it, and the mast's tip sticks out past the sail's top corner. There's no boom and no sheet, so the sail has no lower edge or line holding it, and it looks pasted on, not like canvas.

The picture: the four wheels don't line up as two axles. The two near wheels (lower left and lower middle) are squeezed close together under one side of the deck. The right wheel stands out past the deck edge with no axle or hub joining it to the planks. All the wheels are bare discs with no hub, so nothing holds them on.

The picture: grey stone piles push into the wheels and the deck, one at the lower-left wheel and one under the far rear corner. It looks like the cart is propped on rocks or clipping through them, not standing on its wheels in the sand.

Caption 'a plank deck, four wooden wheels': the deck reads as a skewed parallelogram of boards. Two wheels are half hidden behind it, and from this angle you can't count four or see how they carry it.
Composition: the hut at the right edge is cut off by the frame, and the stone pile and flowers in the foreground take up as much room as the yacht's wheels and deck.
posts.critique: The beach and the light are lovely, but the yacht itself isn't put together: the mast and sail aren't joined to the deck or to each other, and the wheels have no axles and are tangled in rocks. It reads as loose parts set down near each other, not a craft someone built.
